nav.text: You are driving, and your navigation app suggests a route.

closed.text: But there is an emergency ahead, and the road is closed. The app cannot see it. You can.

override.text: So you do not follow it blindly. You take another road. That is what a clinician must be able to do with AI: understand it, question it, and override it.

aug.text: This is augmented intelligence. Automation hands the work to the machine. Augmentation helps the human do the work better.

brings.text: The AI brings speed, pattern detection and consistent calculation. The clinician brings the examination, communication, values, and ethical judgment.

dial.text: So how much should you trust the AI? Picture a dial.

over.text: Turn it all the way up, and you get automation bias: accepting the suggestion just because it looks confident, even when your own evidence disagrees.

comm.text: That leads to commission errors: doing something wrong, because the system suggested it.

omit.text: And omission errors: failing to act, because the system did not warn you.

under.text: Turn it all the way down, and you get under-trust: ignoring support that was correct and useful.

calib.text: The goal is in the middle. Calibrated trust: trust that matches what the system can really do, with healthy scepticism.

over2.text: And for that, oversight has to be meaningful. The clinician needs time, the right information, and the authority to disagree. Not a rubber stamp.
